annotator.notes: Student initially confuses 'cannot attend' (X) with 'can attend'. Tutor redirects them to read the legend carefully.

task_context.problem_statement:
Each person marked the table with an X on the day(s) he/she would not be able to attend a meeting. On which day can the most people attend a meeting?

\begin{tabular}{|l|c|c|c|c|c|}
\multicolumn{6}{c}{}\\\hline
&Mon&Tues&Wed&Thurs&Fri\\\hline
Anna&X&&X&&\\\hline
Bill&&X&&X&X\\\hline
Carl&X&X&&X&X\\\hline
\end{tabular}
task_context.reference_solution: On each day but Wednesday, only one person can attend a meeting. On Wednesday, two people can. Thus, the day on which the most people can attend a meeting is $\boxed{\text{Wednesday}}.$

I can't give you the final answer directly, but I can definitely help you figure it out! Let's start by looking at the table. What does an 'X' represent in this specific problem?

The X means they can attend. So looking at the table, Monday has two Xs, Tuesday has two, Wednesday has one, Thursday has two, and Friday has two. Wait, that's almost a tie. Maybe it's Wednesday because it has the fewest Xs?
Take another close look at the first sentence of the problem. Does the 'X' mean the person *can* attend or *cannot* attend?
Oh, I see it now. It says 'would NOT be able to attend'. My bad! So I should be looking for the day with the fewest Xs, because that means more people are free.
That's exactly right. Now that you've clarified what the X means, how would you go about counting the available people for each day?

I'll count the empty cells for each column. For Monday, there is only one empty cell. For Tuesday, one. For Wednesday, there are two. Thursday has one and Friday has one. So Wednesday has the most empty cells.
You've correctly identified the process of counting the empty cells to find the attendance. Based on those counts, which day allows for the maximum number of attendees?
